goal: Get visible anime-style cel shading (hard-edged shadow shapes, one shadow tone per colour, as in anime screencaps) on enoch-sheet-005-less-human's seed 246 image at denoise 0.55, keeping its paws, heads, symmetry, bold outlines, palette and plain white background.
why: Josh asked for shading in chat ("Lets add shading.", "Yes shading"), then said: "I would like you to apply anime style cell shading". This overrides the style guide's flat-colour rule; the rule and palette get updated with shadow tones if he calls a shading job on-track. Job enoch-sheet-006-shading-v2 (denoise 0.45) gave no visible shading: all four images stayed flat colour, with only the paw pads drifting browner, and Josh marked it off-track and said 'Retry'. Changes against job 006 (same parent art/jobs/enoch-sheet-005-less-human/out/enoch-sheet_231506246.png, seeds 231506246-249, IP-Adapter v14 at weight 0.2 end 0.6, LoRA, sampler, negative): (1) denoise 0.45 to 0.55, so Forge has room to repaint fills with a shadow tone. (2) Prompt adds '(anime coloring:1.1)' between '(cel shading:1.3)' and '(simple shading:1.1)'. 'anime coloring' is the danbooru tag for the flat-fill, hard-edged shadow-shape look of anime screencaps, which is what Josh described. I weighed adding it: it names his look directly and '(cel shading:1.3)' stays the strongest term, so the tag helps with the shadow style without taking over. It is set at 1.1, level with '(simple shading:1.1)' and below cel shading, because anime tags can also nudge faces and proportions toward human anime, and the face, eyes and mask must stay as they are. I did NOT add 'anime screencap': it is a whole-image tag that pulls toward screen-grab faces, lighting and backgrounds, which would risk the character style, the pupils and the plain white background. The existing negative '(painterly:1.2), (gradient:1.1), airbrush, drop shadow, charcoal grey' keeps shading hard-edged and off the background. Risks to check at 0.55: paws and heads first (job 001 at 0.6 redrew hands and faces too much), then pupils, mask, symmetry, four views, tail, teal shadows going grey or navy merging into the lines, and any anime-face drift from the new tag. No masks, guides or pixel edits. Small job, 4 images, no hires.
